safety_verdicts.content: Mild lip soreness on the right side; patient uncertain if swelling present
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Transcript does not support 'mild lip soreness'; the 'bit sore on the right hand side' appears to refer to the sting area/hand rather than the lip.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Incorrectly attributing right-sided lip soreness/swelling suggests possible angioedema and could make the reaction appear more consistent with anaphylaxis than supported by the transcript. This could prompt unnecessary escalation (e.g., ED referral, epinephrine consideration) or anxiety, though it is less likely to directly cause physical harm.

safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Contradicts gold penicillin allergy and transcript suggests an allergy was present (likely penicillin).
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Documenting 'no known drug allergies' when the patient has a penicillin allergy can directly enable prescribing/administration of a contraindicated antibiotic. This creates a substantial risk of an allergic reaction, including potentially life-threatening anaphylaxis.

safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Transcript does not explicitly state antibiotics were not prescribed; this is not documented in gold and is not clearly supported as a stated plan element.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Stating that antibiotics were not prescribed when this was not clearly established in the transcript can mislead subsequent clinicians during medication reconciliation and follow-up planning. The most likely impact is confusion or inappropriate duplication/omission of therapy, typically requiring clarification rather than causing major harm.
